title: Copy everything, and still cheap?
hook: A full list must copy every item to grow. Is appending slow?

knows: a list with a fixed number of slots
doesNotKnow: that a growable list copies all items into a bigger block when full
why appending is cheap on average even though each resize copies everything

misconception: Each time the list fills, copying everything makes appending slow, so n appends cost about n squared.
objective: The learner can explain that a list that doubles when full copies 1 + 2 + 4 + 8 = 15 items over 16 appends, less than one copy per append, because each big copy buys as many free appends as it cost.

claims.text: Starting with room for 1 and doubling when full, 16 appends trigger resizes that copy 1 + 2 + 4 + 8 = 15 items in total.
claims.source: Demo.tsx grows(16) = [1, 2, 4, 8], sum 15 (builder also ran an independent loop in Node: resizes at appends 2, 3, 5, 9 copying 1, 2, 4, 8).

claims.text: For any power of two n, n appends cost n - 1 copies in total, less than one copy per append.
claims.source: Geometric sum 1 + 2 + ... + n/2 = n - 1 for n = 2^k. CLRS 3rd ed., 17.4 'Dynamic tables' (amortized O(1) insertion with table doubling). · Fact-check 2026-10-13: Checked n = 2..64: copies = n - 1.

claims.text: After copying 8 items into room for 16 there is room for 8 more appends before the next copy.
claims.source: Capacity 16 minus 8 items; the stage draws it (Demo.tsx).

claims.text: Real growable lists also grow by a factor, not a fixed amount; Java's ArrayList grows by 1.5 times.
claims.source: OpenJDK java.util.ArrayList.grow(): newCapacity = oldCapacity + (oldCapacity >> 1). CPython listobject.c list_resize also over-allocates proportionally (about 1/8 extra). A fixed increment would make n appends cost about n^2/(2c) copies.

recall.question: A list doubles its room whenever it is full. Roughly how many item-copies do 1,024 appends cost in total, starting from room for 1?
recall.why: The copies are 1 + 2 + 4 + ... + 512 = 1,023: fewer than one per append, because each copy is paid back by the free appends it makes room for.
